We proceed to find an orthogonal basis $B$ of $\text{Col}(A)$ using the Gram-Schmidt process, as follows:

**Step 1.** We set ${v}_{1}={a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$

**Step 2.** We find the vector ${v}_{2}$ orthogonal to $\text{Span}{{v}_{1}}$ using the usual formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{2} & ={a}_{2}-{\text{proj}}_{{v}_{1}}{a}_{2} \\  & ={a}_{2}-\frac{{a}_{2}\cdot {v}_{1}}{{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}}{v}_{1} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]-\frac{6}{6}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3.** We find the vector ${v}_{3}$ orthogonal to $\text{Span}{{v}_{1},{v}_{2}}$ using the usual formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{3} & ={a}_{3}-{\text{proj}}_{{v}_{1}}\,{a}_{3}-{\text{proj}}_{{v}_{2}}\,{a}_{3} \\  & ={a}_{3}-\frac{{a}_{3}\cdot {v}_{1}}{{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}}{v}_{1}-\frac{{a}_{3}\cdot {v}_{2}}{{v}_{2}\cdot {v}_{2}}{v}_{2} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ -1 \\ -4\end{aligned}]-\frac{6}{6}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]-\frac{12}{12}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ -1 \\ -4\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1 \\ -2 \\ -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, 

$$
\frac{b}{c}=\frac{(-1)}{(-2)}=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

v2=a2−projv1a2=a2−a2⋅v1v1⋅v1v1=[321−2]−66[12−10]=[321−2]−[12−10]=[202−2].
